q24763.en: A driver involved in a road accident must stop and help any injured people.

explain.short: The law requires every driver involved in an accident to stop and help the injured. Driving away is a crime (omissione di soccorso).
explain.rule: If you are involved in a road accident you must stop, help any injured people and give your details (name, driving licence, number plate, insurance) to the people who suffered damage. Do not change the traces if they are needed to understand how the accident happened.
explain.trap: 'ha l'obbligo' (must) is right: stopping and helping are duties, not just good manners.

sceneParams.caption: Stop and help the injured

q24764.en: A driver involved in a road accident must give their personal details and the details of their driving licence, number plate and vehicle insurance to the people who suffered damage.

explain.short: The people harmed need these details to get compensation, so the driver must give them.
explain.rule: If you are involved in a road accident you must stop, help any injured people and give your details (name, driving licence, number plate, insurance) to the people who suffered damage. Do not change the traces if they are needed to understand how the accident happened.
explain.trap: 'generalità' means your name and personal details; 'estremi' means the numbers and data of the documents.

sceneParams.caption: Give your details to the damaged party

q24765.en: A driver involved in a road accident must avoid changing the traces, if the dynamics of the accident need to be reconstructed.

explain.short: The police use marks on the road and the position of the cars to understand what happened, so you must not change them when they are needed.
explain.rule: If you are involved in a road accident you must stop, help any injured people and give your details (name, driving licence, number plate, insurance) to the people who suffered damage. Do not change the traces if they are needed to understand how the accident happened.
explain.trap: 'se occorre' (if needed) limits the rule: when there are injured people or a dispute, keep the traces.

sceneParams.caption: Keep the traces of the accident
lines: Do not move or erase the traces

q24766.en: To report the accident to the insurance company, a driver involved in a road accident can use the special pre-printed forms supplied by their own insurer.

explain.short: Insurers give a printed form (the CAI, constatazione amichevole) to fill in after an accident. You can use it to report the claim.
explain.rule: If you are involved in a road accident you must stop, help any injured people and give your details (name, driving licence, number plate, insurance) to the people who suffered damage. Do not change the traces if they are needed to understand how the accident happened.
explain.trap: 'può avvalersi' (can use) is a possibility, not a duty, and it is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Use the insurer's printed form (CAI)

q24767.en: After a road accident it is compulsory to put the warning triangle on the rear window of the vehicle before leaving.

explain.short: The warning triangle goes on the road behind the stopped vehicle to warn traffic. It is not put on the rear window, and you remove it when you leave.
explain.rule: The warning triangle (segnale mobile di pericolo) goes ON THE ROAD behind a vehicle stopped on the carriageway, by day and by night, at a good distance. Outside towns it is compulsory; in towns it is not always required.
explain.trap: 'sul lunotto posteriore' (on the rear window) is the wrong place: the triangle goes on the road.

sceneParams.caption: The triangle goes on the road, not the window
lines: Triangle on the rear window: no
Triangle on the road behind it

q24768.en: After a road accident it is compulsory to cover the vehicle with a plastic sheet.

explain.short: No rule asks you to cover the car. What matters is to help the injured, signal the danger and exchange details.
explain.rule: If you are involved in a road accident you must stop, help any injured people and give your details (name, driving licence, number plate, insurance) to the people who suffered damage. Do not change the traces if they are needed to understand how the accident happened.
explain.trap: 'coprire il veicolo con un telo' (cover with a sheet) is an invented duty.

sceneParams.caption: No duty to cover the car with a sheet
lines: Cover the car with a sheet: no

q24769.en: After a road accident it is compulsory, only at night, to place the warning triangle near the vehicle.

explain.short: The warning triangle is needed by day too: a stopped vehicle on the road is a danger at any hour.
explain.rule: The warning triangle (segnale mobile di pericolo) goes ON THE ROAD behind a vehicle stopped on the carriageway, by day and by night, at a good distance. Outside towns it is compulsory; in towns it is not always required.
explain.trap: 'solo di notte' (only at night) is the trap: the triangle is used by day as well.

sceneParams.caption: Triangle by day AND by night
lines: Use it by day and by night

q24770.en: After a road accident it is compulsory to put the vehicle on the pavement immediately.

explain.short: The pavement is for pedestrians. With damage only you move the cars out of the traffic, but not onto the pavement; with injured people you leave them where they are.
explain.rule: If you are involved in a road accident you must stop, help any injured people and give your details (name, driving licence, number plate, insurance) to the people who suffered damage. Do not change the traces if they are needed to understand how the accident happened.
explain.trap: 'subito sul marciapiede' (at once on the pavement) is wrong twice: not always at once, and never on the pavement.

sceneParams.caption: Never put the car on the pavement
lines: Damage only: clear the road safely

q24771.en: After a road accident it is compulsory to signal the stopped vehicle with the warning triangle even in built-up areas.

explain.short: The warning triangle is a must mainly outside towns. In built-up areas it is not always compulsory, so 'even in towns' as a strict duty is wrong.
explain.rule: The warning triangle (segnale mobile di pericolo) goes ON THE ROAD behind a vehicle stopped on the carriageway, by day and by night, at a good distance. Outside towns it is compulsory; in towns it is not always required.
explain.trap: 'anche nei centri abitati' (even in built-up areas) turns a mainly out-of-town duty into a general one.

sceneParams.caption: In towns the triangle is not always compulsory

q24771.reviewNote: Official answer FALSE; art. 162 CdS on triangle use in built-up areas is nuanced - check the official reasoning.

q24772.en: It is advisable for the driver to service the injection pump of their own vehicle personally.

explain.short: The injection pump is a precise, complex part. Only a specialised workshop should service it.
explain.rule: Keep the vehicle as it was approved: no home-made repairs on complex parts, no changes to engine size or electronics, and fix every fault at once. A warning light that stays on means a problem.
explain.trap: 'personalmente' (personally) is the trap: this job is for a specialist.

sceneParams.caption: Injection pump: specialist workshop only

q24773.en: The distance travelled during the reaction time does not change with speed.

explain.short: During the reaction time the car keeps moving at the same speed. The faster you go, the more metres you cover before you even brake.
explain.rule: Reaction distance = speed x reaction time. If the speed goes up, the distance covered before braking goes up too.
explain.trap: 'non varia' (does not change) is wrong: it grows with speed.

sceneParams.caption: Faster = longer reaction distance
lines: You see a danger and react
Car still moving at full speed

q24774.en: Correct operation of the engine is guaranteed by the red lubricating-oil warning light staying on all the time.

explain.short: The red oil light should go off after starting. If it stays on, the oil pressure is too low: stop and check, or the engine can be damaged.
explain.rule: Keep the vehicle as it was approved: no home-made repairs on complex parts, no changes to engine size or electronics, and fix every fault at once. A warning light that stays on means a problem.
explain.trap: 'costantemente accesa' (always on) means a fault, not a working engine.

sceneParams.caption: Red oil light on = problem, stop

q24775.en: It is allowed to improve the performance of your vehicle by increasing the engine capacity.

explain.short: The vehicle must stay as it was approved and as written in its registration document. Changing the engine size is not allowed freely.
explain.rule: Keep the vehicle as it was approved: no home-made repairs on complex parts, no changes to engine size or electronics, and fix every fault at once. A warning light that stays on means a problem.
explain.trap: 'è consentito' (it is allowed) is wrong: changing the engine size (cilindrata) changes the approved vehicle.

sceneParams.caption: No free changes to engine size

q24776.en: It is not necessary to adjust unbalanced brakes if the driver can correct the vehicle's abnormal behaviour by steering.

explain.short: Uneven brakes pull the car to one side when braking. In an emergency you cannot correct it in time: the brakes must be repaired.
explain.rule: Keep the vehicle as it was approved: no home-made repairs on complex parts, no changes to engine size or electronics, and fix every fault at once. A warning light that stays on means a problem.
explain.trap: 'non è necessario' (it is not necessary) is the trap: unbalanced brakes must always be fixed.

sceneParams.caption: Unbalanced brakes must be repaired
lines: Car pulls to one side when braking

q24777.en: On a slippery road, to get the best grip when braking, it is advisable to press the brake pedal all the way down.

explain.short: On a slippery road a hard brake locks the wheels and the car slides. Brake gently and progressively to keep grip.
explain.rule: On slippery roads brake gently and gradually, keep more distance and lower your speed. Hard braking makes the wheels lock and slide.
explain.trap: 'premere a fondo' (press all the way) is the trap: it causes skidding, not grip.

sceneParams.caption: Slippery road: brake gently

q24778.en: It is allowed to increase the performance of your vehicle by changing the electronic settings of the control unit that manages fuel injection.

explain.short: Changing the engine control unit (centralina) changes the approved vehicle, its emissions and safety. It is not allowed.
explain.rule: Keep the vehicle as it was approved: no home-made repairs on complex parts, no changes to engine size or electronics, and fix every fault at once. A warning light that stays on means a problem.
explain.trap: 'è consentito' (it is allowed) is wrong: chip tuning of the centralina is a forbidden change.

sceneParams.caption: No changes to the engine control unit

q24779.en: When a passenger needs to get in or out, it is advisable to do it on the pavement side or, if there is none, on the side away from traffic.

explain.short: On the pavement side the passenger is away from moving cars, so it is the safest side.
explain.rule: Passengers get in and out only when the vehicle has completely stopped, on the pavement side (or the side away from traffic), opening the door only when it is not a danger for others. Children need an adult's control. No door is ever free of risk.
explain.trap: 'dal lato opposto al traffico' (the side away from traffic) is the right second choice when there is no pavement.

sceneParams.caption: Get out on the pavement side
lines: No pavement: side away from traffic

q24780.en: When a passenger must get in or out of the vehicle, you must open the door only when it causes no danger to other road users.

explain.short: An opened door can hit a cyclist, a motorbike or a pedestrian. Look first and open only when nobody is coming.
explain.rule: Passengers get in and out only when the vehicle has completely stopped, on the pavement side (or the side away from traffic), opening the door only when it is not a danger for others. Children need an adult's control. No door is ever free of risk.
explain.trap: 'solamente' (only) is correct here: the door opens only when it is safe.

sceneParams.caption: Open the door only when it is safe
lines: Open the door only when clear

q24781.en: When a passenger must get in or out of the vehicle, you must make them wait until the vehicle has completely stopped.

explain.short: Getting in or out of a moving car can make the person fall. Wait until the car is completely still.
explain.rule: Passengers get in and out only when the vehicle has completely stopped, on the pavement side (or the side away from traffic), opening the door only when it is not a danger for others. Children need an adult's control. No door is ever free of risk.
explain.trap: 'completamente fermo' (completely stopped) is right: 'almost stopped' is not enough.

sceneParams.caption: Wait until the car has fully stopped

q24782.en: When a child must get in or out of the vehicle, it is advisable that an adult supervises.

explain.short: Children may open the door without looking or run into the road. An adult should control them.
explain.rule: Passengers get in and out only when the vehicle has completely stopped, on the pavement side (or the side away from traffic), opening the door only when it is not a danger for others. Children need an adult's control. No door is ever free of risk.
explain.trap: 'controllo di un adulto' (an adult's supervision) is good advice and correct.

sceneParams.caption: Children get out with an adult watching
lines: Child gets out of the car

q24783.en: When letting a passenger out, you must bear in mind that opening the right-hand door is free of any risk and danger.

explain.short: Even the right door can hit a cyclist, a scooter passing on the right or a pedestrian on the pavement. No door is risk-free.
explain.rule: Passengers get in and out only when the vehicle has completely stopped, on the pavement side (or the side away from traffic), opening the door only when it is not a danger for others. Children need an adult's control. No door is ever free of risk.
explain.trap: 'priva di qualsiasi rischio' (free of any risk) is the trap: there is always some risk.

sceneParams.caption: The right door is not risk-free

q24784.en: If the vehicle sinks into snow or sand and you cannot move it, it is advisable to put something that gives grip (pieces of wood, car mats, etc.) under the spinning wheel.

explain.short: The spinning wheel has no grip. Wood or a car mat under it gives it something to grip so the car can move.
explain.rule: If the wheels spin in snow or sand, put something with grip under the spinning wheel (wood, car mats) and try starting in a higher gear, which gives less force and less spinning. Ice gives even less grip than snow.
explain.trap: 'qualcosa che faccia attrito' (something that gives friction) is the right idea.

sceneParams.caption: Put wood or mats under the spinning wheel
lines: Car stuck in snow or sand
Wood or mat under the wheel

q24785.en: If the vehicle sinks into snow or sand and you cannot start in first gear, it is advisable to engage a higher gear.

explain.short: First gear gives a lot of force to the wheels and they spin. A higher gear gives less force, so the wheels spin less and can grip.
explain.rule: If the wheels spin in snow or sand, put something with grip under the spinning wheel (wood, car mats) and try starting in a higher gear, which gives less force and less spinning. Ice gives even less grip than snow.
explain.trap: 'marcia superiore' (higher gear) sounds strange but is right: less force means less wheelspin.

sceneParams.caption: Stuck: try starting in second gear
lines: Stuck in snow, wheels spin in 1st

q24786.en: On a snowy road the vehicle's grip is lower than on an icy road.

explain.short: Ice is the most slippery surface. Snow gives poor grip, but ice gives even less.
explain.rule: If the wheels spin in snow or sand, put something with grip under the spinning wheel (wood, car mats) and try starting in a higher gear, which gives less force and less spinning. Ice gives even less grip than snow.
explain.trap: 'minore' (lower) is reversed: grip on snow is greater than on ice.

sceneParams.caption: Ice has even less grip than snow

q24787.en: Rear-end collisions happen mainly because of high speed.

explain.short: At high speed you need much more space to stop, so you hit the car in front more easily.
explain.rule: Rear-end collisions (tamponamenti) happen mainly because of high speed, not keeping the safe distance, and driver distraction. They do not depend on the handbrake or on power steering.
explain.trap: 'forte velocità' (high speed) is one of the true main causes.

sceneParams.caption: High speed causes rear-end crashes

q24788.en: Rear-end collisions happen more often if the safe distance is not kept.

explain.short: Too close to the car in front, you have no space to stop when it brakes.
explain.rule: Rear-end collisions (tamponamenti) happen mainly because of high speed, not keeping the safe distance, and driver distraction. They do not depend on the handbrake or on power steering.
explain.trap: 'distanza di sicurezza' (safe distance) is a real cause when it is not respected.

sceneParams.caption: Keep the safe distance

q24789.en: Rear-end collisions happen mainly because of drivers' lack of attention.

explain.short: A distracted driver sees the car in front braking too late.
explain.rule: Rear-end collisions (tamponamenti) happen mainly because of high speed, not keeping the safe distance, and driver distraction. They do not depend on the handbrake or on power steering.
explain.trap: 'disattenzione' (lack of attention) is one of the true main causes.

sceneParams.caption: Distraction causes rear-end crashes

q24790.en: Rear-end collisions happen mainly because of a sudden failure of the parking brake.

explain.short: The parking brake (handbrake) holds the car when parked. Its failure is not what causes rear-end crashes.
explain.rule: Rear-end collisions (tamponamenti) happen mainly because of high speed, not keeping the safe distance, and driver distraction. They do not depend on the handbrake or on power steering.
explain.trap: 'freno di stazionamento' (parking brake) is the wrong cause.

sceneParams.caption: Not the handbrake: speed, distance, distraction

q24791.en: Rear-end collisions happen mainly between motor vehicles with power steering.

explain.short: Power steering only makes steering lighter. It has nothing to do with rear-end crashes.
explain.rule: Rear-end collisions (tamponamenti) happen mainly because of high speed, not keeping the safe distance, and driver distraction. They do not depend on the handbrake or on power steering.
explain.trap: 'servosterzo' (power steering) is an unrelated cause.

sceneParams.caption: Power steering has nothing to do with it

q24792.en: Driving through a long tunnel, when long queues of vehicles form, it is advisable to increase the safe distance, to prevent flames from spreading quickly in case of fire.

explain.short: Cars packed close together let a fire jump from one to the next. More space slows the fire down.
explain.rule: In a long tunnel, keep a bigger distance in queues so a fire cannot spread fast. In a fire, leave the car quickly, follow the signs to the escape routes and safe places, and obey the spoken orders of tunnel staff and firefighters: their orders come first.
explain.trap: 'aumentare la distanza' (increase the distance) is right in tunnel queues.

sceneParams.caption: Tunnel queue: keep a bigger gap

q24793.en: Driving through a long tunnel, in case of fire you must leave the vehicle quickly, following the signs to the escape routes or to safe places protected by fire doors.

explain.short: Smoke fills a tunnel very fast. Leave the car at once and walk to the emergency exits shown by the signs.
explain.rule: In a long tunnel, keep a bigger distance in queues so a fire cannot spread fast. In a fire, leave the car quickly, follow the signs to the escape routes and safe places, and obey the spoken orders of tunnel staff and firefighters: their orders come first.
explain.trap: 'abbandonare velocemente il veicolo' (leave the car quickly) is right: do not stay inside.

sceneParams.caption: Tunnel fire: leave the car, follow exit signs

q24794.en: Driving through a long tunnel, in case of fire you must follow the spoken instructions of the staff or the firefighters, so as not to walk in the wrong direction.

explain.short: Staff and firefighters know where the fire and smoke are, so their spoken orders keep you safe.
explain.rule: In a long tunnel, keep a bigger distance in queues so a fire cannot spread fast. In a fire, leave the car quickly, follow the signs to the escape routes and safe places, and obey the spoken orders of tunnel staff and firefighters: their orders come first.
explain.trap: 'istruzioni vocali' (spoken instructions) of staff and firefighters must be obeyed.

sceneParams.caption: Obey staff and firefighters

q24798.en: Driving through a long tunnel, in case of fire you must follow the emergency signs, even if they clearly contradict the spoken orders given by the firefighters.

explain.short: The firefighters see the real situation, so their orders come before the fixed signs.
explain.rule: In a long tunnel, keep a bigger distance in queues so a fire cannot spread fast. In a fire, leave the car quickly, follow the signs to the escape routes and safe places, and obey the spoken orders of tunnel staff and firefighters: their orders come first.
explain.trap: 'anche se in netto contrasto' (even if clearly against) is the trap: the firefighters' orders win.

sceneParams.caption: Firefighters' orders beat the signs

q24799.en: Motorcycles, having a small frontal outline, are less visible from a distance.

explain.short: A motorbike is narrow seen from the front, so other drivers notice it late.
explain.rule: Motorbikes are narrow, so they are harder to see from far away: watch for them at junctions, when opening doors and in queues (they may pass on the right), and leave a wide side gap when you overtake them. Motorbikes always use dipped headlights, even by day. Noise does not make them more visible, clothing does.
explain.trap: 'meno visibili' (less visible) is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Motorbikes are hard to see from far

q24800.en: Drivers of motor vehicles must, in general, pay special attention to two-wheeled motor vehicles, because they are less easily visible.

explain.short: Since motorbikes are hard to see, car drivers must look for them carefully.
explain.rule: Motorbikes are narrow, so they are harder to see from far away: watch for them at junctions, when opening doors and in queues (they may pass on the right), and leave a wide side gap when you overtake them. Motorbikes always use dipped headlights, even by day. Noise does not make them more visible, clothing does.
explain.trap: 'in generale' (in general) is right: the extra care is always needed.

sceneParams.caption: Watch out for motorbikes

keywords.it: veicoli a motore a due ruote

q24801.en: Drivers of motor vehicles, when opening the doors, must pay special attention to two-wheeled motor vehicles, because they are less visible.

explain.short: A motorbike passing close to a parked car can hit an opening door. Check the mirror before opening.
explain.rule: Motorbikes are narrow, so they are harder to see from far away: watch for them at junctions, when opening doors and in queues (they may pass on the right), and leave a wide side gap when you overtake them. Motorbikes always use dipped headlights, even by day. Noise does not make them more visible, clothing does.
explain.trap: 'nell'aprire le portiere' (when opening doors) is a real danger moment, so it is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Check for motorbikes before opening the door
lines: Parked car, door about to open

q24802.en: When crossing junctions you must always consider that a two-wheeled motor vehicle may arrive, not visible from far, after overtaking the stopped vehicles.

explain.short: A motorbike can pass a queue of stopped cars and appear suddenly at the junction. Always expect it.
explain.rule: Motorbikes are narrow, so they are harder to see from far away: watch for them at junctions, when opening doors and in queues (they may pass on the right), and leave a wide side gap when you overtake them. Motorbikes always use dipped headlights, even by day. Noise does not make them more visible, clothing does.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is right here: this danger can be there at any junction.

sceneParams.caption: Expect a motorbike passing the queue
lines: Junction, cars stopped in a queue

q24803.en: In heavy traffic with queues of vehicles, before opening the doors to get out of your parked vehicle, you must always consider that a two-wheeled motor vehicle may arrive, overtaking the queued vehicles on the right.

explain.short: In a queue, scooters often pass on the right, close to parked cars. Look before you open the door.
explain.rule: Motorbikes are narrow, so they are harder to see from far away: watch for them at junctions, when opening doors and in queues (they may pass on the right), and leave a wide side gap when you overtake them. Motorbikes always use dipped headlights, even by day. Noise does not make them more visible, clothing does.
explain.trap: 'sorpassando a destra' (overtaking on the right) is exactly what scooters do in queues, so it is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Scooters pass the queue on the right: look
lines: Heavy traffic, cars in a queue

q24804.en: When overtaking a two-wheeled motor vehicle, especially at high speed, you must keep a good safe side distance.

explain.short: A motorbike can move sideways because of wind or holes, and a fast car's air flow can push it. Leave a wide gap.
explain.rule: Motorbikes are narrow, so they are harder to see from far away: watch for them at junctions, when opening doors and in queues (they may pass on the right), and leave a wide side gap when you overtake them. Motorbikes always use dipped headlights, even by day. Noise does not make them more visible, clothing does.
explain.trap: 'distanza laterale' (side distance) is the key: give two-wheelers plenty of room.

sceneParams.caption: Wide side gap when passing a motorbike

q24805.en: When riding on the road, to be more visible, motorcycles must keep their dipped headlights on even by day.

explain.short: Motorcycles must always ride with dipped headlights on, day and night, so others see them better.
explain.rule: Motorbikes are narrow, so they are harder to see from far away: watch for them at junctions, when opening doors and in queues (they may pass on the right), and leave a wide side gap when you overtake them. Motorbikes always use dipped headlights, even by day. Noise does not make them more visible, clothing does.
explain.trap: 'anche di giorno' (even by day) is right for motorcycles.

sceneParams.caption: Motorbikes: dipped beam on, day and night
lines: Motorbike on the road by day

q24806.en: When riding in built-up areas, motorcyclists may in any case use the horn when approaching junctions.

explain.short: In towns the horn is allowed only to avoid an immediate danger. Motorcyclists have no special right to use it at every junction.
explain.rule: In built-up areas the horn is used only in case of real, immediate danger, for everyone, motorcyclists included.
explain.trap: 'in ogni caso' (in any case) is the trap: the horn is only for real danger.

sceneParams.caption: Horn in towns only for real danger
lines: Motorbike in town at a junction

q24808.en: On roads where chains are compulsory, when it snows, two-wheeled vehicles are still allowed to ride.

explain.short: Where chains are compulsory in snow, two-wheelers cannot ride safely and cannot fit chains, so they may not ride there.
explain.rule: Where snow chains are compulsory and it is snowing, two-wheeled vehicles may not ride on that road.
explain.trap: 'comunque concesso' (still allowed) is the trap: two-wheelers must stay off that road.

sceneParams.caption: Chains required and snow: no two-wheelers

q24809.en: Motorcycle riders are more easily noticed by car drivers because they are noisier.

explain.short: Noise does not make a motorbike easy to see. Inside a car you often do not hear it, and it stays hard to spot.
explain.rule: Motorbikes are narrow, so they are harder to see from far away: watch for them at junctions, when opening doors and in queues (they may pass on the right), and leave a wide side gap when you overtake them. Motorbikes always use dipped headlights, even by day. Noise does not make them more visible, clothing does.
explain.trap: 'perché più rumorosi' (because noisier) is the false reason.

sceneParams.caption: Noise does not make motorbikes visible
lines: Car driver may not hear it

q24810.en: Riders of two-wheeled vehicles, having a small frontal outline, are more visible from a distance.

explain.short: A small frontal outline makes them LESS visible, not more.
explain.rule: Motorbikes are narrow, so they are harder to see from far away: watch for them at junctions, when opening doors and in queues (they may pass on the right), and leave a wide side gap when you overtake them. Motorbikes always use dipped headlights, even by day. Noise does not make them more visible, clothing does.
explain.trap: 'più visibili' (more visible) is reversed: they are less visible.

sceneParams.caption: Narrow shape = LESS visible

q24811.en: Riders of two-wheeled vehicles, being less easily visible from a distance, must in any case ride with high beams on at night.

explain.short: High beams dazzle oncoming drivers. Like everyone, riders use them only when allowed (no oncoming traffic, no one close ahead), not in any case.
explain.rule: At night two-wheelers use dipped headlights; high beams only outside towns when they do not dazzle anyone.
explain.trap: 'in ogni caso' (in any case) is the trap: high beams would dazzle others.

sceneParams.caption: At night no high beams 'in any case'
lines: High beams in any case: no
Dipped beam; high beam if no one dazzled

q24812.en: A motorcyclist's clothing does not affect their visibility in traffic.

explain.short: Bright or reflective clothes make a rider much easier to see; dark clothes make them harder to see.
explain.rule: Motorbikes are narrow, so they are harder to see from far away: watch for them at junctions, when opening doors and in queues (they may pass on the right), and leave a wide side gap when you overtake them. Motorbikes always use dipped headlights, even by day. Noise does not make them more visible, clothing does.
explain.trap: 'non incide' (does not affect) is wrong: clothing matters a lot.

sceneParams.caption: Bright clothes make riders visible
lines: Rider in dark clothes: hard to see

q24813.en: Tram rails are a road feature that can be dangerous for two-wheeled vehicles.

explain.short: Tram rails are smooth and slippery, so a two-wheeler can lose grip on them.
explain.rule: For two-wheelers, tram rails, painted pedestrian crossings and manhole covers (tombini) are slippery, above all when wet. Go over them slowly and upright, without braking or accelerating hard, and never ride inside the rail groove.
explain.trap: 'può essere pericoloso' (can be dangerous) is correct.

q24819.en: Riding a two-wheeled vehicle on a wet road, braking is particularly dangerous if the wheels are on tram rails, pedestrian crossings or manhole covers.

explain.short: On these slippery spots a wet wheel locks easily when you brake, and the bike falls. Brake before or after them, not on them.
explain.rule: For two-wheelers, tram rails, painted pedestrian crossings and manhole covers (tombini) are slippery, above all when wet. Go over them slowly and upright, without braking or accelerating hard, and never ride inside the rail groove.

q24820.en: Riding fast over manhole covers or tram rails on a two-wheeled vehicle can make it lose road holding and steering control, causing skids or falls.

explain.short: At speed the wheel slips or is deflected by rails and manholes, so the rider can skid or fall. Slow down before them.

q24822.en: When, on a rainy day, you must ride a two-wheeler over tram rails or manhole covers on the road, you must accelerate hard before going over them.

explain.short: Hard acceleration makes the wet wheel spin and slide. Go over them slowly and steadily.
explain.rule: For two-wheelers, tram rails, painted pedestrian crossings and manhole covers (tombini) are slippery, above all when wet. Go over them slowly and upright, without braking or accelerating hard, and never ride inside the rail groove.
explain.trap: 'accelerare decisamente' (accelerate hard) is the trap: it causes a slide.

q24823.en: When, on a rainy day, you must ride a two-wheeler over tram rails or manhole covers on the road, it is good to stand up on the footrests before going over them.

explain.short: Standing up makes the bike less stable and helps nothing. Stay seated, upright and calm.

q24824.en: When, on a rainy day, you must ride a two-wheeler over tram rails or manhole covers on the road, it is good to do it in a wheelie, so that the front wheel, which steers, does not go over them.

q24826.en: If you have to ride a two-wheeled vehicle on a carriageway shared by vehicles and trams, it is good, if possible, to ride with both wheels inside the groove of the tram rail.
